Palette The game styles — title cards, credits and logos — keep the game's own colours, so the palette does not apply to them.
Recolours the letters only, never the background. The custom picker derives the whole ramp — shadow, highlight, outline — from one face colour, snapped to the Genesis palette's 36-step channels.

Background
Transparent stays transparent in PNG, WebP and AVIF.
Intro
Plays the scene's own opening ahead of the text, the way its game does — the S&K Death Egg landing, the S3 island, the AIZ fly-in, the Sonic 1 and 2 title screens coming up. Off starts on the scene at rest.
Music
The scene's own music, from the frame its game starts it: the song is run through the game's sound driver ahead of time, and the page plays what the driver sent the YM2612 and PSG on chips of its own, frame for frame with the animation. With it on, playback and video run to the end of the song, the scene idling on as its title screen does. WebM and MP4 carry it; GIF and APNG have no sound and keep to the animation's own length.
Text position 176 Output locks to the Genesis frame, 320×224. Each scene starts the text where its game puts its own — on S3 and S&K that is 176, where & KNUCKLES sits.

Timebase
GIF delays are whole centiseconds, so it can hit PAL exactly (100 frames at 2cs = 2.00s) but can only approximate NTSC by resampling to 83 frames (1.66s). APNG delays are a fraction, so it expresses 59.92 Hz exactly as 100/5992 — pick APNG if the timing matters. Video is a real-time capture and is approximate either way.
Defaults are read from Obj_TitleBanner_Main in the Sonic 3 & Knuckles disassembly: 96px entry, 4px/frame initial velocity, 0.25px/frame² spring, velocity halved on each zero crossing. Stock values settle in 100 frames.
GIF and APNG are exact and lossless. WebM and MP4 are lossy real-time captures — WebM keeps transparency, MP4 does not (H.264 has no alpha, so transparent areas go black; pick a background colour first).
Sprite sheet ripped by DarkNic the Half Demon1234 — credit kept as asked.
Sonic the Hedgehog, Sonic the Hedgehog 2, Sonic the Hedgehog 3 and Sonic & Knuckles are © Sega. This is an unofficial fan tool; the artwork belongs to them. The scenes and the game lettering are decoded from the Sonic Retro disassemblies.
Character set: A–Z, 0–9, space and ! " # $ % & ' ( ) * + , - . / : ; < = > ? @ [ \ ] _ ` { | } ~ — everything on a standard keyboard. ^ is the sheet's triangle rather than a caret.
The ROM has no font at all — it stores & KNUCKLES as a flat 168×24 bitmap — so only & C E K L N S U trace to real game pixels. The rest of the alphabet was reconstructed by the ripper; the digits were built here from the sheet's own shading rules.
